identity.description: Discord: chat and communications platform. Its developer docs (docs.discord.com, formerly discord.com/developers) cover the REST API, Gateway WebSocket, OAuth2, webhooks and bots. Confirmed as the Discord product.
identity.identity_notes: Discord developer docs at docs.discord.com/developers describe the Discord API, OAuth2 and bot tokens. The 301 redirect from discord.com/developers/docs points to docs.discord.com, which is the same vendor's docs.

auth.oauth_flows: Authorization code grant, implicit grant (discouraged), client credentials (for testing). Refresh via refresh_token grant. Bot users use a bot token from the app settings, not OAuth2.
auth.token_refresh: Access tokens expire; refresh tokens are issued with the authorization code flow and can be exchanged with a refresh_token grant. Implicit grant issues no refresh token.
auth.scopes_notes: Some OAuth2 scopes require approval from Discord to use.

access.production_restrictions: Privileged intents (Message Content, Server Members, Presence) must be approved for apps in 100+ guilds (verification); some OAuth2 scopes require Discord approval. These block production scale, not test credentials.

api.rate_limits: Excessive requests are rate-limited; users who regularly hit and ignore limits have API keys revoked. Specific numbers not established.
api.limitations: Resource coverage not established from fetched pages. Bot/webhook/OAuth2 surfaces confirmed; full endpoint list not fetched. Privileged intents require approval at scale. Webhook names cannot contain 'clyde' or 'discord'.

claims.value: docs.discord.com/mcp returned HTTP 405 on GET, and a search summary describes it as an official docs-search MCP server
Multiple community Discord MCP servers exist, and a DEV Community roundup says Discord has no official MCP server

open_questions: Is docs.discord.com/mcp a Discord-published MCP server? A 405 on GET is consistent with an HTTP MCP endpoint, but no page content was retrieved to confirm. Discord's docs/MCP page should be checked directly.
Full REST resource list (guilds, channels, messages, members, roles, interactions) was not established. The reference fetch returned only the base URL, not endpoints. Breadth is therefore unknown.
Exact base URL https://discord.com/api was seen in a code block but no verbatim sentence was captured for it.
Whether a free developer account is required and whether a test server incurs any cost was not verified against Discord's own pages.
Gateway specifics (intents list, connection limits) and SDK ecosystem (official vs community libraries such as discord.js, discord.py) were not confirmed from fetched pages.
Whether a trial or sandbox exists was not established. Discord uses a test server rather than a sandbox, as far as the sources show.

rationale: Self-serve test credentials (free self serve) and a documented REST/WebSocket interface.
